<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

</span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We build upon <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span>, a procedure designed to align text embedding spaces without parallel data. <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> finds a near-perfect alignment, but it is expensive and unstable. We present <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mini-vec2vec</span>, a simple and efficient alternative that is highly robust and incurs a much lower computational cost. Moreover, the learned mapping is a linear transformation. Our method consists of three main stages: a tentative matching of pseudo-parallel embedding vectors, transformation fitting, and iterative refinement. Our linear alternative exceeds the original instantiation of <span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> by orders of magnitude in efficiency, while matching or exceeding their results. The method’s stability and interpretable algorithmic steps facilitate scaling and unlock new opportunities for adoption in new domains and fields.</p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><a href="https://github.com/guy-dar/mini-vec2vec" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">

<span class="ltx_inline-block fas fa-github" aria-hidden="true">
</span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter"> github.com/guy-dar/mini-vec2vec</span>
</a></p>
</div>

<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Representation learning has revolutionized natural language processing by producing embedding models that capture rich semantic structure in high-dimensional vector spaces. These learned representations encode complex linguistic relationships, enabling downstream tasks such as semantic similarity and information retrieval. However, different models, training procedures, or even different random initializations of the same architecture can produce embedding spaces that, while semantically meaningful, are not directly comparable due to arbitrary rotations, reflections, and translations in their coordinate systems.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The problem of aligning embedding spaces without parallel supervision – that is, without access to pairs of embeddings that represent identical semantic content – has emerged as a fundamental challenge with far-reaching implications. Successful unsupervised alignment has multiple implications across many domains: multilingual natural language processing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Conneau et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, cross-modal alignment between text and image representations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maniparambil et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and privacy concerns <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song and Raghunathan, 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Morris et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The recent <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> method <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jha et al., 2025</a>)</cite> demonstrated that unsupervised alignment is indeed possible using CycleGAN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, an adversarial training framework. Their approach is theoretically grounded in the <span id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Platonic Representation Hypothesis</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huh et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, which posits that well-trained representations, regardless of their specific architectures or training procedures, tend to converge toward geometrically similar spaces. Under this hypothesis, semantic relationships are preserved across models in terms of relative distances and angles, suggesting that alignment should be achievable through geometric transformations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">While <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span> has proven effective, adversarial training frameworks bring inherent challenges that limit their practical applicability. GANs are notoriously computationally intensive, requiring careful hyperparameter tuning and often exhibiting training instability characterized by mode collapse, oscillatory behavior, or failure to converge <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Saxena and Cao, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Goodfellow, 2017</a>)</cite>. These methods typically demand substantial computational resources, including GPU acceleration and large amounts of training data – factors that may prohibit their utilization by most researchers and users.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Our point of departure is still universal geometry, but we pursue a different approach. We are motivated by the remarkable success of supervised alignment approaches, particularly neural network stitching methods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lenc and Vedaldi, 2015</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bansal et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, which have demonstrated that simple affine transformations often suffice to align representations. Unfortunately, stitching requires access to pairs of matching representations. Our key methodological insight is that with universal geometry, structural similarities should be detectable and exploitable, even without adversarial training. Specifically, the relative arrangement of semantic clusters, the preservation of neighborhood structures, and the overall geometric organization of concepts should provide sufficient signal for alignment, even in the complete absence of parallel supervision. To this end, we utilize the Relative Representation framework of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Moschella et al. (2023)</a></cite>, which allows us to operate in a universal space agnostic of arbitrary coordinate systems.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Our contribution is <span id="S1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mini-vec2vec</span>, a simple and robust pipeline with competitive alignment performance offering several key advantages over adversarial approaches: computational efficiency (running on commodity CPU hardware), training stability (deterministic components with controllable stochastic elements), interpretability (each step has a clear geometric interpretation), and sample efficiency (effective with substantially fewer training examples). Through comprehensive experiments, we demonstrate that this simple approach not only matches but often exceeds the performance of the more complex adversarial method while requiring orders of magnitude less computational resources.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Preliminaries</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The hypothesis that neural networks converge to geometrically similar representations has been explored across multiple domains and scales. Early work by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Olah (2015)</a></cite> revealed striking structural regularities in representations of different convolutional networks, showing distances between object representations are roughly the same regardless of architecture. These findings suggested that the geometric organization of learned features might be more universal than previously assumed. The <span id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Platonic Representation Hypothesis</span>, formally articulated by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huh et al. (2024)</a></cite>, represents the most comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding universal geometry. The hypothesis posits that well-trained representations converge toward a shared geometric structure that reflects the underlying structure of the data domain.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Moschella et al. (2023)</a></cite> operationalized the observations of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Olah (2015)</a></cite> and proposed <span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">relative representations</span> as a mathematically principled framework for comparing latent spaces. Their key insight was that while absolute coordinates may vary arbitrarily across models, relative similarity structures – captured through pairwise distances to a shared set of anchor data points – remain remarkably stable. This work provided both a theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for the existence of model-agnostic geometric properties.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Given a set of anchor points <math id="S2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{a}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{a}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> in an embedding space, the relative representation of any point <math id="S2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as:</p>
<table id="S2.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x})=[f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{a}_{1}),f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{a}_{2}),\ldots,f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{a}_{k})]^{T}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐚</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐚</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x})=[f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{a}_{1}),f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{a}_{2}),\ldots,f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{a}_{k})]^{T},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is a similarity function (typically cosine similarity). Two representations from different models will have close relative representations if they represent similar objects.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg2" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 2</span> </span> Algorithm for creating pseudo-pairs using noisy anchors</figcaption>
<div id="alg2.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="algx2.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">1:</span></span>
            
            
          Normalized embeddings <math id="algx2.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{A},\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{A},\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, clusters <math id="algx2.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, neighbors <math id="algx2.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, runs <math id="algx2.l1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2:</span></span>
            
            
          Set of pseudo-parallel pairs <math id="algx2.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
            
            
          Initialize collections: <math id="algx2.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{A}\leftarrow[],\mathcal{R}_{B}\leftarrow[]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{A}\leftarrow[],\mathcal{R}_{B}\leftarrow[]</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="algx2.l4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="algx2.l4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="algx2.l4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="algx2.l4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span> <span id="algx2.l4.5" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="algx2.l4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Multiple runs for robustness
</span>
</div>
<div id="algx2.l5" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">5:</span></span>
            
            
            Cluster both spaces: <math id="algx2.l5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{c}^{A}_{i,j}\}\leftarrow\text{k-means}(\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{A})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐜</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>k-means</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{c}^{A}_{i,j}\}\leftarrow\text{k-means}(\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{A})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="algx2.l5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{c}^{B}_{i,j}\}\leftarrow\text{k-means}(\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{B})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐜</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>k-means</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>B</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{c}^{B}_{i,j}\}\leftarrow\text{k-means}(\hat{\mathbf{X}}_{B})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l6" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">6:</span></span>
            
            
            Compute similarities: <math id="algx2.l6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{S}^{A},\mathbf{S}^{B}\leftarrow\text{cosine similarities between centroids}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐒</mi><mi>A</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐒</mi><mi>B</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mtext>cosine similarities between centroids</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{S}^{A},\mathbf{S}^{B}\leftarrow\text{cosine similarities between centroids}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">7:</span></span>
            
            
            Find correspondence: <math id="algx2.l7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}^{*}_{i}\leftarrow\text{solve QAP}(\mathbf{S}^{A},\mathbf{S}^{B})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐏</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>solve QAP</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐒</mi><mi>A</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐒</mi><mi>B</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}^{*}_{i}\leftarrow\text{solve QAP}(\mathbf{S}^{A},\mathbf{S}^{B})</annotation></semantics></math> using multiple 2-OPT runs

</div>
<div id="algx2.l8" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">8:</span></span>
            
            
            Build relative representations: <math id="algx2.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i},\mathbf{r}^{B}_{i}\leftarrow\text{cosine similarities to anchors}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mtext>cosine similarities to anchors</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i},\mathbf{r}^{B}_{i}\leftarrow\text{cosine similarities to anchors}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l9" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l9.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">9:</span></span>
            
            
            Store: append <math id="algx2.l9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i},\mathbf{r}^{B}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i},\mathbf{r}^{B}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="algx2.l9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{A},\mathcal{R}_{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{A},\mathcal{R}_{B}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l10" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l10.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">10:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="algx2.l10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="algx2.l10.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>
</div>
<div id="algx2.l11" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l11.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">11:</span></span>
            
            
          Concatenate: <math id="algx2.l11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}^{A}\leftarrow\text{concatenate all runs in }\mathcal{R}_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>A</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>concatenate all runs in </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}^{A}\leftarrow\text{concatenate all runs in }\mathcal{R}_{A}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l12" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l12.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">12:</span></span>
            
            
          Concatenate: <math id="algx2.l12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}^{B}\leftarrow\text{concatenate all runs in }\mathcal{R}_{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>B</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>concatenate all runs in </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}^{B}\leftarrow\text{concatenate all runs in }\mathcal{R}_{B}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l13.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">13:</span></span>
            
            
          Match embeddings: <math id="algx2.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}_{k}(\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i})\leftarrow\text{find }k\text{ nearest neighbors from }\mathbf{r}^{B}\text{ to each }\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext>find </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> nearest neighbors from </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>B</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> to each </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}_{k}(\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i})\leftarrow\text{find }k\text{ nearest neighbors from }\mathbf{r}^{B}\text{ to each }\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l14" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l14.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">14:</span></span>
            
            
          Create pseudo-pairs: <math id="algx2.l14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}\leftarrow\left\{(\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i},\frac{1}{k}\sum_{j}\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}):\mathbf{r}^{B}_{j}\in\mathcal{N}_{k}(\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i})\right\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}\leftarrow\left\{(\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i},\frac{1}{k}\sum_{j}\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}):\mathbf{r}^{B}_{j}\in\mathcal{N}_{k}(\mathbf{r}^{A}_{i})\right\}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l15" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l15.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">15:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="algx2.l15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="algx2.l15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Problem Formulation</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow the setup laid out in <span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span>. We assume access to two pools of text embeddings, each from a different encoder, and our task is to align their embedding spaces without paired examples. Similar to <span id="S3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">vec2vec</span>, we learn a <span id="S3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">parameterized</span> mapping (neural network or linear transformation) rather than a one-to-one matching between data points. This approach offers key advantages:</p>
<ul id="S3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Generalization:</span> New embeddings can be translated without re-applying the algorithm</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Robustness:</span> Works when one-to-one point matching doesn’t exist, requiring only similar data distributions</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Out-of-distribution capability:</span> The parameterized nature enables generalization beyond the training data</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The universal geometry hypothesis indicates that such a task can be possible: “good enough” models learn equivalent geometries where cosine similarities remain approximately invariant across embedding spaces. These geometric similarities enable the identification of this alignment.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}_{A}=\{\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n_{A}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}_{A}=\{\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n_{A}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}_{B}=\{\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{n_{B}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}_{B}=\{\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{n_{B}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote two sets of <math id="S3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional embeddings, where <math id="S3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i},\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i},\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. These embeddings represent semantic content from potentially different models, architectures, or training procedures, but we assume they encode similar semantic information from the same underlying distribution <math id="S3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>. Unlike more traditional setups, there <span id="S3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">does not exist</span> a pairing between data points, i.e., there is no overlap between the sentences themselves.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We organize these embeddings into matrices <math id="S3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}_{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{A}\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}_{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{A}\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{B}\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{B}\times d}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each row corresponds to a single embedding vector. The fundamental challenge is that while both spaces may contain similar semantic structures, they are related by an unknown transformation.
Our goal is to learn a transformation function <math id="S3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i})\approx\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i})\approx\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> represent similar semantic content. More generally, the setup allows for learning a pair of functions <math id="S3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{1},f_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{1},f_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> sending embeddings to a third space, such that <math id="S3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{1}(\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i})\approx f_{2}(\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{1}(\mathbf{x}^{A}_{i})\approx f_{2}(\mathbf{x}^{B}_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>. We will not take advantage of this flexibility in the paper.<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          Of course, <math id="footnote1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{1}(x)=f_{2}(x)=\text{const}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>const</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{1}(x)=f_{2}(x)=\text{const}</annotation></semantics></math> would be a trivial solution, without additional constraints. So, similarity needs to be evaluated in comparison to other vectors in the dataset.</span></span></span></p>
</div>

</div>
<div id="algx4.l8" class="ltx_listingline">

</div>

Bold indicates best performance. Underline indicates nearly equally good performance (<math id="S3.T1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 0.01</annotation></semantics></math> difference). Bold and underline combined indicate better performance, but only within a <math id="S3.T1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math> margin.
